classification.difficultyReason: The student differentiates a quintic and factorises 10x^3(x-2) to find x=0 and x=2. The second-derivative test classifies x=2 but gives f''(0)=0, so they must switch to a first-derivative sign table to classify x=0. That fallback is the extra demand over p40-q12, where f'' settles every point. It is still easier than p39-q10, which needs a chain-rule derivative, a messier second derivative and two inconclusive points. The graph supplied also helps a little.

content.prompt: Find and classify the stationary points on $f(x)=2x^5-5x^4$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=10x^4-20x^3\\10x^3(x-2)&=0\\x&=0,\ 2\\f(0)&=0\\f(2)&=64-80\\&=-16\\f''(x)&=40x^3-60x^2\\f''(2)&=320-240\\&=80>0\\f''(0)&=0\end{aligned}$$

There is a minimum at $(2,-16)$. At $x=0$, the second-derivative test is inconclusive. Use a table of slopes:

$x$	$-1$	$0$	$1$
$f'(x)$	$30$	$0$	$-10$

The gradient changes from positive to negative, so there is a maximum at $(0,0)$.
